mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last three weeks (-23.4 to -12.4), indicating a steady return to in-office work that increases incidental weekday retail and dining visits, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -23.4 to -12.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend for the same period.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -18 points week-on-week, it signals a meaningful uptick in commuter and shopper transit usage that precedes a rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks, as transit hubs feed foot traffic to adjacent retail precincts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -18 points for the current week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -22.6 to -18.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -18 points, or declines despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a compounding return-to-routine effect: commuters re-entering offices via public transit generate overlapping retail visits (lunch, errands, after-work shopping), producing a larger joint lift to RETAIL_REC than either series alone over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no larger than what single-series models (WORKPLACES-only or TRANSIT-only) predict, or RETAIL_REC falls despite joint improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined modestly each week (9.0 to 7.3), indicating households are spending marginally less time at home; this behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity directly substitutes into retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.0 to 7.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following week despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline, implying the substitution effect is absent.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS swing (-6.9 to -20.1 to -13.9) shows volatile outdoor-recreation substitution; when PARKS mobility drops sharply week-on-week, suppressed residents redirect leisure time toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -6.9 to -20.1 between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 8 points, or moves in the same direction as PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery across WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects easing of pandemic-era restrictions in NSW; if this policy-driven loosening continues, retail capacity limits and trading-hour restrictions are further relaxed, allowing RETAIL_REC to keep climbing over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain above t-3w levels for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show net improvement over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines despite continued WORKPLACES/TRANSIT recovery, indicating policy easing is not the binding driver.

mechanism_narrative: The decision point falls in mid-December, immediately preceding the Christmas and summer holiday period in Sydney; historical seasonal shopping surges plus summer outdoor activity typically lift RETAIL_REC sharply in the following two weeks regardless of current trend levels.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-12-15, within the pre-Christmas shopping window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks spanning Christmas despite the seasonal shopping window, indicating seasonal effects are overridden by other factors.

mechanism_narrative: If the emerging summer holiday regime drives residents to travel away from metropolitan Sydney for leave over late December, local RETAIL_REC in the metro area will fall over the next four weeks as the usual customer base temporarily relocates, even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show recovery.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES plateaus or declines going into late December
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-12-15 precedes summer holiday travel period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite falling RESIDENTIAL and flat/declining WORKPLACES, indicating holiday travel is not drawing residents away from local retail.
